blocks.text: Setting up your Mac for inventory management

Google Sheets does not have a native Mac app. It runs in your browser. For the best experience, use Google Chrome. You can create a shortcut that acts like an app. Open your sheet in Chrome. Click the three-dot menu in the top right corner. Select Cast, Save, and Share. Then select Install page as app. This puts an icon in your dock. It opens in its own window. This stops you from losing your inventory sheet in a sea of browser tabs.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for inventory managers

Speed matters when you are updating stock levels. Use these shortcuts to move faster. Press ⌘ + / to see all shortcuts. Use ⌘ + ⇧ + H to find and replace item names. If you need to hide a column of sensitive pricing data, use ⌘ + ⌥ + 0. To hide a row, use ⌘ + ⌥ + 9. These small actions save minutes every hour.
Keep your data clean and accurate

Inventory data breaks easily. One typo in an SKU can ruin your count. Use Data Validation to force users to pick from a list. Go to Data > Data validation. Choose Dropdown. This ensures every entry matches your master list. Use Conditional Formatting to highlight low stock. Go to Format > Conditional formatting. Set a rule for cells less than 10 to turn red. This gives you a visual alert before you run out of stock.

Google Sheets can handle up to 20 million cells. Large files can still get slow. Avoid complex formulas in every single cell. Use ARRAYFORMULA to calculate totals in one place. Keep your raw data on one tab. Use a separate tab for your dashboard. This keeps the calculation load low. If the sheet feels sluggish, clear out unused rows and columns.

You likely work with a team. Keep your data safe with correct sharing settings. Click the Share button in the top right. Give your team View only access if they only need to see stock levels. Only give Editor access to people who need to update counts. Check the revision history often. Go to File > Version history > See version history. This shows you who changed a cell and when.

faq.question: Can I use Google Sheets offline on my Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. You must enable offline access in your Google Drive settings while connected to the internet. Then you can edit your sheets without a connection.

faq.question: Is there a native Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No. Google Sheets is a web-based tool. You can use the PWA method described above to create a desktop shortcut that behaves like an app.
